basis.governing_question: Should Quinta Azul enter the retail markets of Spain, France, Germany and Poland, and in which order?

phases.name: Research
phases.objective_one_line: Assess each retail market's attractiveness and Quinta Azul's ability to win there, and shortlist the markets for entry design.

gate.label: Findings sign-off
gate.decision: Which markets go forward into entry design, and which stop here?

phases.name: Design
phases.objective_one_line: Define entry options and business cases per shortlisted market, and set the entry sequence and roadmap.

gate.label: Final readout
gate.decision: Approve the go/no-go per country and the entry sequence?

workstreams.name: Market screen
workstreams.answers: Which of the four countries look attractive enough on desk data to assess in full?
activities: Gather desk data on retail olive-oil demand per country
Screen the four markets on size, growth and access
Propose the markets to assess in full

workstreams.name: Market attractiveness
workstreams.answers: How large, how fast-growing and how attractive is each shortlisted country's retail market for Quinta Azul's olive oil?
activities: Size retail demand and growth, two markets at a time
Review consumer purchase data and category reports
Compare the markets on agreed attractiveness criteria

workstreams.name: Competitors and access
workstreams.answers: Which competitors, retail channels and regulations shape Quinta Azul's access to each shortlisted market?
activities: Map competitors and retail channels in each market
Review regulations that apply to olive-oil retail sales
Interview retail buyers on listing terms and rivals

workstreams.name: Capability to win
workstreams.answers: Does Quinta Azul have the assets and capabilities to win in each shortlisted market?
activities: Interview Quinta Azul staff who run sales and production
Analyze Quinta Azul's volume, cost and price data
Assess the gaps to win in each shortlisted market

workstreams.name: Entry options
workstreams.answers: Which ways of entering each shortlisted market are open to Quinta Azul, and how do they compare?
activities: List the entry routes open to Quinta Azul in each market
Compare the routes on criteria agreed with the sponsors
Test the routes with retail buyers and Quinta Azul staff

workstreams.name: Business cases
workstreams.answers: What would entering each shortlisted market return and require, and does it support a go or no-go?
activities: Build the business case for each market's preferred option
Model volumes, costs and returns from Quinta Azul's data
Set out the evidence for a go or no-go in each country

workstreams.name: Entry sequence and roadmap
workstreams.answers: In what order, and with what roadmap, should Quinta Azul enter the countries that are a go?
activities: Compare entry orders on timing, effort and risk
Draft the entry roadmap for the countries that are a go
Test the sequence with the CEO and Commercial Director

deliverables.name: Desk screen of the four retail markets
Interim retail demand and growth sizing
Competitor and retail channel map by market
Retail regulation and buyer listing findings
Findings pack for the shortlist decision
Entry roadmap for the countries that are a go
Go/no-go and entry sequence decision pack

events.label: Kick-off
events.purpose: Start the assessment and secure access
events.decision: Which data and people at Quinta Azul will be open to the research from week 1?
agenda: Present the question, the four markets and the 15-week plan
Align on the evidence needed for each go or no-go decision
Confirm access to data and people for the first weeks

events.label: Workshop: first findings
events.purpose: Review first findings on the four markets
events.decision: Which markets should the remaining research examine in full detail?
agenda: Present the desk screen and the interim demand and growth sizing
Review the competitor and retail channel map by market
Decide which markets the remaining research examines in detail

events.label: Findings sign-off
events.purpose: Decide which markets move into entry design
events.decision: Which markets go forward into entry design, and which stop here?
agenda: Present attractiveness, regulation, listing and capability findings
Review the findings pack for the shortlist decision
Decide which markets go forward into entry design

events.label: Check-in: design progress
events.purpose: Check progress before the final readout
events.decision: Is the work on track for the final readout, or should the remaining scope change?
agenda: Present progress on entry options and business cases
Review the emerging substance the final readout will cover
Discuss open points to settle before the final readout

events.label: Final readout
events.purpose: Approve go/no-go per country and sequence
events.decision: Approve the go/no-go per country and the entry sequence?
agenda: Present entry options and business cases by market
Review the entry roadmap and the go/no-go decision pack
Decide the go/no-go per country and the entry sequence

architect_notes: Length is not given, so the 11 to 15 weeks are an estimate (work sizes at 11 to 17); confirm it before quoting.
Research and Design sit mid-estimate; slow buyer-interview access or client review rounds would push them to 10 and 7 weeks.
Assumes three of the four markets are assessed in full after the desk screen; assessing two would cut Research by 2 to 3 weeks.
A market dropped at the desk screen gets its no-go on desk evidence only; confirm that meets the go/no-go criterion.
Go or no-go for any country stopped at the Research gate rests on the desk screen or full assessment, not a business case.

sub_questions.question: How large and attractive is each country's retail market for Quinta Azul's olive oil?
Which competitors, retail channels and regulations shape Quinta Azul's access to each market?
Does Quinta Azul have the assets and capabilities to win in each market?
Which entry option and business case support a go or no-go for each of the four countries?
In what order, and with what roadmap, should Quinta Azul enter the countries that are a go?

drivers.evidence: retail markets of Spain, France, Germany and Poland

phases.name: Research

work.unit: Market assessed in full (demand, channels, competitors, regulation, buyer interviews)

phases.why: Four screened at once, three assessed in full two at a time; the desk screen before full work exceeds typical 4 to 8 weeks.

phases.name: Design

work.unit: Entry option and business case for one market
Entry sequence and roadmap across markets

phases.why: Three business cases built two at a time, then one sequence and roadmap; top of the range exceeds typical 3 to 6 weeks.

sizing.levers: Assessing two markets in full instead of three, or running all three at once, would shorten Research most.
